text:
anna: quick heads-up — while onboarding magnet-16b-int8 yesterday I saw a consistent replay divergence when using anchor priming > 8k tokens. thought it might be noise but reproducer attached.

anna: repro steps: run replay_trace on a long doc (~12k tokens) with anchor=8192 then resume with sliding window. int8 profile. observe token shift around 9.1k.

mike: can you paste the small log snippet?

anna: sure —
```
[2024-11-29 14:02:13] replay:start model=magnet-16b-quant-int8 anchor=8192 prime=12288
[2024-11-29 14:02:16] kv:prefill ok keys=8192
[2024-11-29 14:02:17] gen:step token_idx=9142 kv_index=9142 out_token=\"the\"
[2024-11-29 14:02:17] mismatch:expected=\"the\" got=\"a\"
```

jamie: interesting — looks like a RoPE phase wrap at the anchor boundary. did you try forcing rotary_scale=1.0 vs 0.9995?

anna: yes. with rotary_scale=1.0 the mismatch moves ~+4 tokens (later), with 0.9995 it moves earlier. quant vs fp16 behaves differently — fp16 baseline had no mismatch.

devon: probable culprit: int8 quantized matmul + interpolation of rotary sin/cos tables when reconstructing positions beyond anchor. we saw similar but smaller in magnet-13b onboarding.

mike: can perf-bot run the automated microbench that compares anchor vs sliding priming across quant configs? @perf-bot run anchor-replay-batch --models magnet-16b,magnet-13b --quant int8,int4,f16 --anchors 4096,8192,12288 --replay-seed 42 --output /tmp/replay_cmp.json

perf-bot: Received request to run anchor-replay-batch. Queued on runner-4. ETA ~7m. Command: scripts/bench/anchor_replay.py --models magnet-16b,magnet-13b --quant int8,int4,f16 --anchors 4096,8192,12288 --seed 42 --out /tmp/replay_cmp.json :gear:

perf-bot: Partial results (first 3 anchors):
- magnet-16b int8 anchor=4096: pass (no divergence)
- magnet-16b int8 anchor=8192: divergence @ mean token 9128 (std 6) across 5 trials
- magnet-16b int8 anchor=12288: divergence @ mean token 11840 (std 12)
- magnet-16b f16 anchor=8192: no divergence in 10 trials

jamie: thanks — that pattern strongly correlates with anchor window crossing. does the divergence magnitude scale with anchor size? looks like it does.

anna: I also diffed kv keys around the break: some keys at positions ~9130 differ by a small l2 of 0.003 which accumulates into token-change. not a full corruption but drift.

devon: hypothesis: quant rounding + prefix interpolation error in sin/cos table generation for high positions creates slight phase offset. with long prefix the offset accumulates through attention and flips next-token logits.

mike: practical ask: is this an onboarding showstopper? for Dedicated customers we need to guarantee deterministic resume across priming modes. options: 1) disable anchor priming above X for quant profiles, 2) tweak rotary reconstruction to use double precision for sin/cos table then cast back, 3) add tiny calibration step that measures phase offset and corrects.

jamie: i can try option (2) quickly — generate sin/cos in fp32/f64, store table in fp16 or int8-packed later. might cost a bit of memory but keep inference path unchanged.

anna: experiment idea: run a short calibration pass that computes delta phase per head for positions [anchor-64..anchor+64] and injects a head-wise phase correction into kv on resume. cheap and non-invasive.

devon: that aligns with previous mitigation we used for shard boundary jitter. i'll sketch a prototype in prefill code.

mike: timeline? this week if possible. also capture eval impact: compute perplexity delta on our long-doc goldset and token-level alignment rate.

anna: will run a quick check: script below —
```bash
python -m bench.replay_calibrate --model magnet-16b --quant int8 --anchor 8192 --goldset data/longdoc_gold.jsonl 
# outputs: /tmp/calibration_8192.json with head_phase_corrections
```

anna: results so far: calibration reduced divergence from mean 9128 -> 12000+ (i.e., mostly pushed out of test window) and alignment rate improved from 96.1% -> 99.7% on goldset (5 trials).

jamie: promising. mike, do we accept calibration as default for int8 onboarding or require algo change?

mike: for short-term, enable calibration flag for quant profiles and add test to onboarding checklist. long-term, follow up with rotary reconstruction in compile/runtime to avoid bookkeeping hacks. open a ticket for runtime change.

devon: i'll PR prototype for the calibration hack to eng-ml branch; add unit tests that replay a fixed seed across fp16/int8 and assert alignment > 99%.

anna: created a small GH gist with logs + command: https://gist.github.com/anon/adb1234 (contains traces and quickplot).

mike: ack. thanks team. tagging @onboarding-pm for visibility. :wave:

perf-bot: Run complete. Full artifact: /artifacts/anchor_replay_1701352468.tar.gz

anna: putting notes into model-onboarding checklist and will attach perf plots. if anyone sees other longctx/quant gotchas ping here.

mike: good work — we'll roll calibration into canary for dedicated testbeds next Monday.
